comment: ‘Capture once, governed well, made available’ is a helpful antidote to duplicate reporting, but it can imply that all data should be captured at the finest level and reused indefinitely. In health, data are contextual: purpose, granularity, timeliness, provenance and lawful basis affect fitness for reuse. We are wary as this phrase may unintentionally encourage excessive collection and function creep.

reviewer.name: Brian O'Donnell (on behalf of HISP-UiO)
reviewer.organisation: HISP Centre at University of Oslo

anchor.note: p.21 l.429–459 read as the printed page; section 1.5 agrees

public.text: ‘Capture once, governed well, made available’ is a helpful antidote to duplicate reporting, but it can imply that all data should be captured at the finest level and reused indefinitely. In health, data are contextual: purpose, granularity, timeliness, provenance and lawful basis affect fitness for reuse. We are wary as this phrase may unintentionally encourage excessive collection and function creep.
public.suggestedRevision: Replace with: ‘Collect minumum needed; govern transparently; and reuse only where lawful, necessary, and fit for the new purpose.’ Add that aggregate-first collection may be appropriate and that secondary use requires purpose-specific governance and disclosure controls.
